notation.meaning: College and non-college labor supply in efficiency units

blocks.md: **The log relative supply of college to non-college labour rose by about 1.5 log points between 1963 and 2017 — fast until the early 1980s, then at roughly half the pace.**
Measured as $\ln(H_t/L_t)$ relative to 1963, in [Efficiency Units of Labor](note:efficiency-units-of-labor). Values read off the chart, approximate.
Implied average growth: roughly 4.5% a year from 1963 to 1982, and roughly 2% a year from 1982 to 2017.

The supply slowdown around 1982 lines up with the start of the rapid rise in the [Skill Premium](note:skill-premium). The [Canonical Model of the Skill Premium](note:canonical-model-of-the-skill-premium) attributes much of the premium's *deviation from trend* to these supply swings.

- [US Skill Premium Since 1963](note:us-skill-premium-since-1963)
- [Relative Supply and Demand](note:relative-supply-and-demand)
- Paper: [Katz and Murphy 1992 - Changes in Relative Wages](note:katz-and-murphy-1992-changes-in-relative-wages)
